prompt:
I need the front end for Slotroom. A stockroom layout and slotting tool for small online shops that run their own warehouse unit, showing where every product lives so the team can decide where incoming stock should go.

Who's using it: Priya, co-owner and operations lead of Fernhollow Goods, a six-person online shop selling houseplants, ceramic planters and plant-care supplies. She does the packing herself on busy days and knows every corner of the unit.

What they're doing right now: A holiday shipment of 340 units of a new speckled stoneware planter in three sizes arrives Thursday, and it's expected to be the season's best seller. She needs to decide where it goes in the 2,400 sq ft unit. Ideally that's close to the packing bench so pickers walk less, but the nearest shelves are full of slow-moving fertilizer stock, and the large size is too heavy for the top shelves. She's comparing open spots by distance from packing, shelf height and weight limits, and thinking about moving the fertilizer to the back wall to free up the prime bays.

What's in the system at this point: One warehouse unit with a roll-up door on the north wall, a packing bench and shipping scale in the northeast corner, and a fragile-goods zone along the east wall. Six aisles (A–F), 4 shelf levels each, 212 bins with dimensions (e.g. 48×24×18 in), weight limits (150 lb lower levels, 60 lb top) and current fill (0–100%). 186 active SKUs, each with its bin location, units on hand and picks in the last 30 days (e.g. 'Ceramic Planter Speckle 6in': not yet stocked; 'Liquid Fertilizer 8oz': 410 units in bins A1-1 to A1-3, 22 picks/month; 'Pothos Cutting Kit': 96 picks/month in D3-2). Walking distance from each bin to the packing bench ranges from 12 to 96 feet. Incoming shipment: 120 small (1.8 lb each), 140 medium (3.6 lb), 80 large (7.9 lb), in 18 cartons.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
